analysis.title: Texas Turns Blue, Futures Turn Green: Why Wall Street Bought The Biggest Democrat Wave Since 1993
key_insights: Nasdaq 100 futures fell as much as 2.4% and S&P futures 1.4% overnight as Democratic wins mounted, then recovered to Nasdaq futures +0.9% and S&P futures +1% by morning in New York, a roughly 929-point round trip in NDX futures. KOSPI fell more than 4% at the low.

Democrats won seven Senate seats (IA, KS, ME, NC, OH, SC, TX) against a needed net gain of four. Decision Desk HQ had the Senate at 54-44 with Alaska and Mississippi uncalled. NBC projects about 258 House seats for Democrats, the most since 1993. No veto-proof majority.

Goldman's Mike Cahill reads the vote as a Republican revolt plus motivated Democrats rather than progressive outperformance. Democrats are winning rural areas Trump took by 10-15 points. He attributes this to tariffs, gas prices and ICE activity in south Texas. He argues larger majorities with red-district moderates could reduce the progressive wing's power.

Texas Democrat Gina Hinojosa beat Greg Abbott with roughly 53% and said she will not lift the data center permit freeze until more comprehensive regulation passes. Cahill says this could push gigawatts due online in 2027 to 2028. IREN, Hut 8 and Applied Digital traded lower premarket while hyperscalers rose.

Goldman's Rich Privorotsky attributes the rebound to positioning. Hedges placed in recent days now need to be monetized, AI infrastructure multiples are already de-rated, and he expects vol to struggle to hold a bid. VXN is 30.5 against a March peak of 33.5. His view is that AI infrastructure has been sold to death and vol likely falls quickly, which drives spot higher in the short term.

Privorotsky sees two implications of constrained data center supply. Suppliers of chips, cooling and electrical equipment risk customers having over-ordered relative to capacity they can energize. Scarcity raises the value of existing energized compute, which benefits hyperscalers and owners of deployed capacity.

Deutsche's George Saravelos calls the outcome risk positive. A large Democratic majority plus Trump's stated willingness to work with the opposition should act as a brake on extreme policy and lower risk premia. He sees negative time decay on oil as Iran re-escalation is delayed, and the debt ceiling (binding by Q2 2027) as the main remaining domestic policy uncertainty.

Saravelos expects lower energy and policy risk premia plus higher AI implementation risk to weaken the dollar on balance and support a continued bottoming in EUR/USD. A lame-duck failure to raise the debt ceiling before January would be an added dollar negative.

Cross-asset moves: the 10Y yield fell as much as 7bps to about 4.89% then returned to about 4.93%. DXY fell and USDJPY dropped from above 158.70 to below 157.50. Goldman's Asia sales desk reported a firm USD selling bias from macro hedge funds and CTAs. Gold rose 2.3% to $4,020. Bitcoin returned to the prior day's highs.
AMD's quarter was described as a blowout, with the stock up about 6% premarket, supporting AI bulls.

Privorotsky cites the S&P 500 being higher 12 months after all 19 midterm elections since 1950 and expects CEOs to pull capex, permitting and M&A into 2027. The author expects the hedge unwind to carry stocks a few sessions and views permits, power and the debt limit as the harder problems in January. That view is the author's and not a bank's.

Trump told the New York Times he would work with Democrats, then posted a hat with the word veto.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's Privorotsky says hedges need to be monetized, AI infrastructure is de-rated, and vol should fall, driving spot higher. The S&P 500 was higher 12 months after all 19 midterms since 1950. Deutsche sees lower risk premia from divided government.
tension_points.bear_case: The author says the Texas data center freeze, the debt ceiling binding by Q2, Iran strike risk and Trump's veto posture were not priced out. He expects the rally to be the easy part, with permits, power and the debt limit arriving in January.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A failure by the lame-duck Congress to raise the debt ceiling before January, which Saravelos would count as an added dollar negative, or a US strike on Iran.

tension_points.bull_case: Privorotsky says scarcity of energized compute raises its value, benefiting hyperscalers and owners of deployed capacity, and pricing could stay higher for longer.
tension_points.bear_case: Suppliers of chips, cooling and electrical equipment risk over-ordering relative to energizable capacity, and Texas could delay gigawatts from 2027 to 2028.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hinojosa lifting the Texas permit freeze only after comprehensive regulation passes, which could take much longer than the end-of-year expectation.
